encounters.cc: Secondary amenorrhea for 6 months following dilation and curettage procedure

lines: Secondary amenorrhea for 6 months following dilation and curettage procedure
She reports having regular menstrual cycles until she underwent a dilation and curettage for a missed abortion one year ago.
Since the procedure, her menstrual flow has gradually decreased and eventually ceased.
She denies any hot flashes, vaginal dryness, or changes in libido.
- History of Hodgkin lymphoma, in remission since adolescence
- History of ovarian Sertoli-Leydig cell tumor, status post unilateral oophorectomy
- Dilation and curettage for missed abortion
- Vaginal delivery, first child, complicated by postpartum hemorrhage
- Hydrocortisone 20 mg PO every morning; 10 mg PO every evening
- Estradiol/norethindrone acetate 1 mg/0.5 mg PO daily
- Calcium carbonate 600 mg PO twice daily
She has no known drug allergies.
Smoking: Never smoker. Alcohol: None. Occupation: High school mathematics teacher.
On physical examination, her vital signs are within normal limits,
Her abdominal and pelvic examinations are unremarkable.
Laboratory tests reveal normal serum prolactin, thyroid-stimulating hormone, and follicle-stimulating hormone levels.
Transvaginal ultrasonography shows a thin endometrial lining with scattered areas of echogenicity within the uterine cavity suggestive of adhesions.
A progesterone challenge test fails to induce bleeding.

encounters.cc: Six-month history of progressive hirsutism, deepening voice, and amenorrhea

lines: Six-month history of progressive hirsutism, deepening voice, and amenorrhea
Patient returns six months after Asherman syndrome evaluation with prior Sertoli-Leydig cell tumor.
She reports significant hair loss on her scalp in male-pattern distribution and an increase in muscle mass despite not changing her exercise routine.
- History of Hodgkin lymphoma, in remission since adolescence
- History of ovarian Sertoli-Leydig cell tumor, status post unilateral oophorectomy
- Dilation and curettage for missed abortion
- Vaginal delivery, first child, complicated by postpartum hemorrhage
- Hydrocortisone 20 mg PO every morning; 10 mg PO every evening
- Estradiol/norethindrone acetate 1 mg/0.5 mg PO daily
- Calcium carbonate 600 mg PO twice daily
She denies the use of anabolic steroids or supplements.
On physical examination, she has temporal balding, a prominent Adam's apple, and clitoromegaly.
An abdominal ultrasound shows a 3 cm mass in the right ovary.

lines: Follow-up evaluation for progressive hirsutism and menstrual irregularity with suspected ovarian mass

The patient with history of Sertoli-Leydig cell tumor returns for follow-up of progressive hirsutism and suspected ovarian mass, presenting with a 6-month history of increasing facial hair, deepening of her voice, and cessation of her menstrual periods.
She denies any use of anabolic steroids or supplements.
- History of Hodgkin lymphoma, in remission since adolescence
- History of ovarian Sertoli-Leydig cell tumor, status post unilateral oophorectomy
- Dilation and curettage for missed abortion
- Vaginal delivery, first child, complicated by postpartum hemorrhage
- Hydrocortisone 20 mg PO every morning; 10 mg PO every evening
- Estradiol/norethindrone acetate 1 mg/0.5 mg PO daily
- Calcium carbonate 600 mg PO twice daily
Smoking: Never smoker. Alcohol: None. Occupation: High school mathematics teacher.
On physical examination, she has increased muscle mass, clitoromegaly, and temporal balding.
Her blood pressure and the rest of the physical examination are normal.

encounters.cc: Difficulty becoming pregnant for 18 months with irregular menses for three years

lines: Difficulty becoming pregnant for 18 months with irregular menses for three years
The patient with Asherman syndrome and status post unilateral oophorectomy for ovarian Sertoli-Leydig cell tumor presents for evaluation of infertility and menstrual irregularity.
She reports that her menstrual cycles, which were previously regular since menarche at age 12, started becoming irregular and infrequent about three years ago.
Over the past year, she has had only two menstrual periods.
She denies weight changes, excessive exercise, galactorrhea, or signs of androgen excess.
- History of Hodgkin lymphoma, in remission since adolescence
- History of ovarian Sertoli-Leydig cell tumor, status post unilateral oophorectomy
Her past medical history includes treatment for Hodgkin lymphoma during adolescence, including chemotherapy and radiation.
- Dilation and curettage for missed abortion
- Vaginal delivery, first child, complicated by postpartum hemorrhage
- Hydrocortisone 20 mg PO every morning; 10 mg PO every evening
- Estradiol/norethindrone acetate 1 mg/0.5 mg PO daily
- Calcium carbonate 600 mg PO twice daily
She has no significant family history of reproductive disorders.
She does not smoke or drink alcohol
On physical exam, her BMI is 21 kg/m².
She has normal secondary sexual characteristics and no hirsutism or acne.
Pelvic exam shows a small, mildly atrophic uterus with no adnexal masses.
Laboratory studies show normal TSH and prolactin, low estradiol, and elevated serum FSH and LH levels.
Transvaginal ultrasound reveals reduced ovarian volume and a paucity of developing follicles.

encounters.cc: Persistent heavy vaginal bleeding 30 minutes after home vaginal delivery

lines: Persistent heavy vaginal bleeding 30 minutes after home vaginal delivery
The patient with panhypopituitarism from prior postpartum hemorrhage, Asherman syndrome, and prior oophorectomy presents with heavy vaginal bleeding.
Her pregnancy was complicated by gestational diabetes, which was diet-controlled.
Labor was induced at 41 weeks, and she reports that the active phase of labor lasted approximately 18 hours.
The newborn's weight was 4300 g (9.48 lb).
- History of Hodgkin lymphoma, in remission since adolescence
- History of ovarian Sertoli-Leydig cell tumor, status post unilateral oophorectomy
- Dilation and curettage for missed abortion
- Vaginal delivery, first child, complicated by postpartum hemorrhage
- Hydrocortisone 20 mg PO every morning; 10 mg PO every evening
- Estradiol/norethindrone acetate 1 mg/0.5 mg PO daily
- Calcium carbonate 600 mg PO twice daily
Smoking: Never smoker. Alcohol: None. Occupation: High school mathematics teacher.
On examination, her blood pressure is 100/60 mmHg, heart rate is 110 beats per minute, and temperature is 37.2°C (99°F).
The uterus is palpated abdominally and is noted to be soft and enlarged.
There is no foul-smelling discharge or signs of trauma to the genital tract.
The estimated blood loss is 800 mL.

encounters.cc: Persistent fatigue, lightheadedness, and difficulty breastfeeding one month after delivery

lines: Persistent fatigue, lightheadedness, and difficulty breastfeeding one month after delivery

The patient with a history of Hodgkin lymphoma in remission, Asherman syndrome, premature ovarian insufficiency, and status post unilateral oophorectomy for ovarian tumor returns to Endocrinology one month after vaginal delivery of her first child complicated by significant blood loss requiring transfusion.
Since delivery, she reports feeling lightheaded when standing, generalized weakness, and has had difficulty producing breast milk despite frequent attempts.
Her appetite is poor, and she has noticed that she has not regained her menstrual cycles since childbirth.
- History of Hodgkin lymphoma, in remission since adolescence
- History of ovarian Sertoli-Leydig cell tumor, status post unilateral oophorectomy
- Dilation and curettage for missed abortion
- Vaginal delivery, first child, complicated by postpartum hemorrhage
- Hydrocortisone 20 mg PO every morning; 10 mg PO every evening
- Estradiol/norethindrone acetate 1 mg/0.5 mg PO daily
- Calcium carbonate 600 mg PO twice daily
Smoking: Never smoker. Alcohol: None. Occupation: High school mathematics teacher.
On examination, her blood pressure is 96/64 mmHg while sitting and 78/58 mmHg upon standing
She appears thin and pale but is alert and oriented.
Cardiovascular and respiratory examinations are normal.
There is no evidence of edema or hyperpigmentation.

encounters.cc: Follow-up 6 weeks after emergency cesarean delivery for persistent fatigue and lactation failure

lines: Follow-up 6 weeks after emergency cesarean delivery for persistent fatigue and lactation failure

The patient returns for follow-up six weeks after emergency cesarean delivery with persistent fatigue and lactation failure, with established history of panhypopituitarism secondary to prior postpartum hemorrhage.
Her pregnancy was uncomplicated, but the delivery was prolonged and complicated by uterine atony and heavy blood loss requiring transfusion.
Since returning home, she has felt persistently fatigued and lightheaded, especially when standing.
She also notes that her breasts have remained soft, and she has been unable to produce milk despite trying to breastfeed regularly.
She reports irregular meals due to decreased appetite and describes feeling mentally foggy.
She has not had any vaginal bleeding since the delivery and attributes that to breastfeeding.
Fetal growth and postpartum evaluation of the infant are normal.
- History of Hodgkin lymphoma, in remission since adolescence
- History of ovarian Sertoli-Leydig cell tumor, status post unilateral oophorectomy
She has no past medical conditions.
- Dilation and curettage for missed abortion
- Vaginal delivery, first child, complicated by postpartum hemorrhage
- Hydrocortisone 20 mg PO every morning; 10 mg PO every evening
- Estradiol/norethindrone acetate 1 mg/0.5 mg PO daily
- Calcium carbonate 600 mg PO twice daily
She does not smoke, drink alcohol, or use drugs
Vital signs include temperature 98.0°F (36.7°C), blood pressure 90/62 mm Hg, and heart rate 76/min
On exam, she appears pale and tired.
Breast exam reveals no engorgement or nipple discharge.
Skin is dry, and capillary refill is normal.
There are no focal neurologic findings.
